subject: Legacy usage allocation — EU domicile split & payment reallocation
messages:
From: Natalie Ortiz <natalie.ortiz@acmecloud.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>; finance@acmecloud.io
Cc: Oliver Huang <oliver.huang@aws-partner.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Legacy billing applied to non‑EU entity — request to reallocate

Hi Sean —

We dug into our April–May marketplace invoices and noticed ~€45k of legacy usage that was routed to our global (US) invoice rather than our EU‑domiciled billing entity. That creates VAT exposure for us and our accounting team is asking Redwood to: (1) reallocate the covered usage to the EU entity, (2) issue a credit memo to reverse the US charge, and (3) provide an evidence bundle for VAT auditors (usage IDs + invoice mapping).

I've attached a preliminary CSV (acme_legacy_usage_ids.csv) that flags the usage IDs we believe are affected and a copy of invoice_202704.pdf for reference. Can you confirm whether Redwood can perform reallocation for legacy marketplace lines and what steps/timeline look like?

Thanks — appreciate quick guidance here.

—Natalie Ortiz
Head of Cloud Finance, AcmeCloud
finance@acmecloud.io

Attachment: acme_legacy_usage_ids.csv (CSV stub, 1.2MB)
Attachment: acme_invoice_202704.pdf (PDF stub, 420KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Ortiz <natalie.ortiz@acmecloud.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Legacy billing applied to non‑EU entity — request to reallocate

Thanks Natalie — looping in Marissa (marketplace reconciliation) and Karthik (metering engineering) to validate the root cause and next steps. Monica, FYI for credits/collections coordination.

Quick asks to help us move faster:
- Can you confirm the legal entity name + VAT number for the EU invoice target?
- Is the CSV you attached the canonical list of usage IDs to reallocate, or do you anticipate more lines after a full ledger pull?
- Does Acme want the credit memo applied to the next invoice or issued as an immediate standalone refund?

Marissa/Karthik — initial read appears like a project tag mismatch during a late onboarding mapping change (we've seen similar when project->entity tags didn't propagate to the marketplace metering bridge). If you can validate, please include an estimated execution window and whether a retro write (invoice reissue + credit memo) is possible without tax-team escalation.

Sean
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Ortiz <natalie.ortiz@acmecloud.io>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Legacy billing applied to non‑EU entity — request to reallocate

Natalie — thanks for the data, that CSV helped. Initial reconciliation notes below:

Summary of findings
- Total impacted lines in CSV: 127 usage IDs (~€45,120) tied to three marketplace SKUs.
- Root cause candidate: onboarding mapping rule change on 2027‑04‑02 that left older usage tied to the global/default entity.

What Redwood can do operationally
1) Reallocation approach: create a credit memo against the original US invoice lines and reissue equivalent lines on the EU billing entity. This will generate a credit + new invoice (taxed per EU VAT rules).
2) Timeline options:
   - Express (7–10 business days): we run the automated reallocation script and prepare credit memo + new invoice; requires Acme signoff on CSV and VAT number.
   - Standard (3–4 weeks): add manual QC to reduce risk of double‑billing for cross‑project usage.
3) Evidence bundle: we can produce a CSV mapping (usage_id -> original_timestamp -> new_invoice_id) and export raw metering logs for auditors.

Dependencies and blockers
- Need legal entity name + EU VAT ID from Acme.
- If you require the credit memo as an immediate refund (payment reversal) instead of invoice credit, we need collections/finance signoff (Monica) and marketplace payment partner approval.

Next steps we request from Acme
- Confirm EU billing entity details and VAT number in reply.
- Confirm preferred timeline (Express or Standard).
- Sign off on the attached reallocation proposal CSV once we send it.

I'll prepare a preliminary reallocation_proposal.csv and an internal change ticket once we have signoff.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Marketplace Billing Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (will send reallocation_proposal.csv after signoff)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>; Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Ortiz <natalie.ortiz@acmecloud.io>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Legacy billing applied to non‑EU entity — request to reallocate

Hi all — I ran a ledger-level join between Acme's CSV and our metering table. Quick technical findings (summary):

- Confirmed ~127 IDs flagged by Acme match entries with entity_id = "global-default" in our metering bridge between 2027‑03‑15 and 2027‑04‑05.
- Of those, 18 usage IDs have downstream aggregation into consolidated multi-project lines (we need to special-case those to avoid orphaned invoices).
- Proposed safe approach: script that updates historical nominal attribution to the EU entity in our billing reconciliation layer only (not changing raw meter events), then generate credit memo + reissue invoice. This keeps raw telemetry unmodified for audit, but fixes billing rollups.

Estimated runtime & risks
- Script runtime: ~3 hours for execution + 1 business day for QC and invoice generation (Express path).
- Risk: if we reassign IDs that have been previously partially invoiced via reseller flows, we may need partner coordination (looping Oliver from AWS).

I'll prepare the reallocation_proposal.csv that flags the 18 special‑case IDs and a recommended handling strategy. If Acme confirms EU VAT and Express path, we can schedule for next Wednesday 2027‑06‑30 evening UTC to avoid impacting live bill generation.

-Karthik
Metering Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: reallocation_proposal.csv (CSV stub, 560KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Ortiz <natalie.ortiz@acmecloud.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Legacy billing applied to non‑EU entity — request to reallocate

Natalie — thanks for confirming details in the HubSpot ticket earlier today (HC‑99812). Per Acme's reply: EU legal entity is AcmeCloud Europe LTD, VAT GB123456789. Acme prefers the Express path and wants the credit memo applied as a standalone credit (not a refund) to be visible on their July statement.

Marissa/Karthik/Monica — please proceed with the Express execution plan:
- Karthik: run the reallocation script on 2027‑06‑30 UTC evening as proposed; send the mapping CSV to Acme and myself.
- Marissa: prepare the credit memo + new EU invoice and generate the evidence bundle (usage_id -> original_invoice -> new_invoice). Share DocuSign credit memo link so Acme's finance can sign.
- Monica: confirm collections will not block applying a standalone credit to July statement and confirm whether any merchant/partner approvals are needed for immediate crediting.

Natalie: please confirm you will sign the DocuSign credit memo when we send it. Once the DocuSign is signed we will mark the action items as scheduled and provide a final ETA.

I'll keep this thread as the single source of truth for status updates. Thanks team.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
